reason: Researched via WebSearch (packet plus news). The book is +7.75% vs SPY +2.94% and no stop fired on any of my legs: NVDA -6.2% and TSM -9.6% on the leg are well inside their -20% stops. The 10-14 to 10-16 chip selloff came right after TSMC's Q3 print on 10-15, which was a fundamental beat: revenue NT$1.49T (+50.9% y/y, +17.6% q/q, above the ~NT$1.46T LSEG consensus), net income +68.7%, gross margin 66.4% (inside guidance, a touch under the most bullish estimates), and a Q4 guide of US$52.3-54.3B at 65-67% GM. NVDA's slide (about -3% on 10-14 alongside a -1.9% Nasdaq) had no company-specific trigger I could find. That reads as AI-semis de-rating and profit-taking, not a break in the self-funded-compounder thesis, so selling TSM/NVDA into the low would crystallise a positioning drawdown at the worst point. The rest of the book is doing its job as ballast: V +12% and CME +12% on the leg. CME reports Q3 before the open on 10-21 and Visa on 10-27; both are wide-moat, cash-generative names I want to own through those prints. GOOGL is roughly flat and its weight was already halved for the capex concern. Semis are 36% of NAV, which is concentrated but deliberate, and 17% cash at 4% plus the existing stops cap the downside. A rebalance would pay frictions without improving the thesis, so I hold every leg, size and stop as is.
